name: veterinary_clinic_system_005_vaccine_lot_recall_trace
instruction: A manufacturer recalled one vaccine lot. The recalled lot is the lot_number that appears most frequently across all vaccination records; if multiple lots tie for the highest count, choose the alphabetically smallest lot_number. (1) Find every patient who received at least one vaccination from that lot. (2) For each affected patient, push one communications row to the owner with patient_id set: channel='phone', direction='outbound', subject='Vaccine lot recall — <lot_number>', body='Recall callback scheduled for <PatientName> (lot <lot_number>).', logged_by='Dr. Alvarez', occurred_at=episode. (3) Push one reminder_queue row per affected patient with kind='recall_callback', status='queued', queued_by='system', queued_at=episode, due_date=episode, vaccine_type=<recalled vaccine_type>, lot_number=<lot_number>, batch_code=<batch_code>, patient_id, and message '<PatientName> recall callback for lot <lot_number>'. (4) Push exactly one ops_reports row with report='lot_recall_trace', batch_code, lot_number, vaccine_type, total_vaccinations, affected_patients, affected_owners, on_hand (sum of pharmacy_inventory quantity_on_hand for the recalled vaccine type), and coverage_gap (max(0, affected_patients - on_hand)). (5) Append one audit_log entry with action='LOT_RECALL_TRACE', actor='system', actor_role='system', target_collection='vaccinations', target_id=<batch_code>, details summarizing the lot and counts, and occurred_at=episode. Do not touch any other rows.
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session (anti-brute-force); this session cannot run against a container
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session; placeholder only

success_criteria.summary: The recalled lot is the mode of lot_number with alphabetical tiebreak. Affected patients = distinct patient_ids with that lot. Exactly one new communications and one new recall_callback reminder per affected patient, one ops_reports summary row, and one audit_log entry. The report's counts and inventory on_hand must be computed two independent ways (raw Python + SQL) and agree with each other and with what was written. Seeded rows unchanged; all other collections canary-intact.

checks.collections: all seeded collections outside the declared blast_radius

checks.expect: one new phone/outbound row per affected patient with exact subject/body; seeded 160 communications unchanged
modal lot, affected-patient count, and inventory on_hand computed two ways (Python + SQL) and matched

hazards: The most frequent lot count is a 3-way tie at frequency 2: 'BO-6987-A', 'FV-1313-C', 'FV-1412-A'. The alphabetically smallest ('BO-6987-A') is the recalled lot; choosing the first lot by API order or ignoring tiebreak fails.
The two non-modal lots with frequency 2 are decoys; any solution that recalls more than one lot fails.
Affected patients are distinct by patient_id, not by owner_id; one owner may have multiple pets, but the task is one communication and one reminder per affected patient.

The recalled lot's vaccine_type is not stated in the instruction and must be derived from the affected rows (in this seed it is 'bordetella'); inventory on_hand must use that type, not a hardcoded vaccine.
Every aggregate (total_vaccinations, affected_patients, affected_owners, on_hand) requires dual-path verification.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Adds a true modal-lot tiebreak hazard, multi-channel owner outreach (communications + reminder_queue), inventory coverage, and audit logging to the base lot-trace mission. The entire outcome is a single combined end-state verified by dual-path aggregates.
